42912648.text: Bladder diverticula are predisposed to developing intradiverticular bladder tumors. We describe FDG PET/CT findings in a case of intradiverticular bladder cancer. At FDG PET/CT (62 min), the intradiverticular bladder cancer appeared as an exophytic lesion with similar density to the urine in the bladder‌ and intense activity mimicking a bladder diverticulum. At delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT (275 min), the tumor showed higher density and activity than the urine in the bladder, consistent with malignancy. This case indicates that delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT may be necessary for detecting possible intradiverticular bladder cancer in patient with bladder diverticulum.

42966148.label: Purpose
42966148.text: To compare after-hours emergency CT report turnaround during periods with versus without roster-recorded on-site CT radiologist availability.

42966148.label: Materials and methods
42966148.text: This retrospective roster-based cohort included emergency-department CT examinations from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The common-support cohort comprised non-holiday weekdays from 15:00 to 06:59 and all weekends and public holidays. Components within 15 min were grouped into packages. The exposure was on-site CT radiologist availability recorded in the final as-worked duty roster; actual reporting route was secondary. The primary outcome was scan-to-complete-report turnaround time (TAT). Models used duty-date-clustered standard errors and adjusted for patient, temporal, workload, and examination characteristics.

42966148.label: Results
42966148.text: The cohort contained 13,533 CT packages; 13,270 had usable TAT and 12,333 index encounters were clinically linked. Median TAT was 81 min without and 58 min with an on-site radiologist. Absence of an on-site radiologist was associated with 33.9% longer adjusted TAT (95% CI 25.4-43.0). The association was 28.4% for routine non-contrast head CT and 45.5% for abdominopelvic CT (interaction + 15.1%; p = 0.001). A ± 120-minute staffing-boundary analysis estimated 45.7% longer TAT (16.3-82.5), with positive estimates across ± 60- to ± 180-minute bandwidths and no detected covariate discontinuities. Actual-route TAT was 47.7% longer amid 34.5% route discordance.

42966148.label: Conclusion
42966148.text: During comparable after-hours periods, roster-recorded absence of an on-site CT radiologist was associated with longer complete-report TAT, particularly for abdominopelvic CT. Downstream stay differences were exploratory and may reflect broader hospital processes.

42984198.text: Noninvasive imaging-based diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in high-risk patients currently relies on the radiological hallmark of arterial-phase hyperenhancement followed by delayed washout. These criteria were designed to achieve both a high positive predictive value and sufficient specificity when applied to well-defined target populations. However, the incidence of HCC is rising globally among individuals outside the traditional high-risk groups, including those with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) and genetic predispositions. This shifting epidemiology poses challenges to the current noninvasive diagnostic strategies and the binary classification of patients as either "at high-risk" or "not at high-risk," which heavily depends on established risk factors such as chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and liver cirrhosis. Consequently, HCC in non-high-risk individuals is often diagnosed at more advanced stages, underscoring the urgent need for reliable and noninvasive diagnostic tools tailored to this demographic population. These challenges present opportunities for the radiology community to play a proactive role in addressing them. Given the heterogeneous risk factors among low- and intermediate-risk populations, integrated strategies incorporating imaging features, fibrosis stage, serum biomarkers, individualized risk models, and artificial intelligence-assisted cross-sectional imaging may help improve the noninvasive diagnosis of non-cirrhotic or metabolically driven HCC. This review summarizes the current performance and limitations of noninvasive diagnosis outside the conventional high-risk populations in the era of MASLD and highlights emerging diagnostic strategies that warrant further investigation as evidence continues to accumulate.

43045948.label: Background
43045948.text: Auger electron (AE) therapy is expected to be especially efficient for metastatic disease due to the highly localized energy deposition of AE-emitters. Lanthanum-135 (135La) has been proposed as a candidate for AE therapy since it has beneficial radiochemical characteristics and a high AE yield. In this proof-of-principle study, we investigated internalizing (DOTA-TATE) and non-internalizing (DOTA-LM3) SSTR2 vectors labeled with 135La in the in vitro CA20948 model for neuroendocrine tumors.

43045948.label: Results
43045948.text: Reproducible and traceable activity measurements were challenging due to extensive non-linearity and measurement geometry effects, which was attributed to a substantial low-energy X-ray yield of 135La. The maximum molar activity that could be achieved was 50 MBq/nmol with a radiochemical conversion and purity of > 99% for [135La]La-DOTA-TATE, while this was ~ 97% and ~ 93%, respectively, for [135La]La-DOTA-LM3. The cellular biodistribution of both radioligands in CA20948 cells corresponded to previous reports with 177Lu- and 161Tb-labelled peptides. Despite small changes in KD and Bmax of [135La]La-DOTA-LM3, compared to other radiolanthanide-labeled peptides, they remained within a comparable range. The absorbed dose to the cell nucleus was too low to elicit a therapeutic effect for both [135La]La-DOTA-TATE and [135La]La-DOTA-LM3 (< 0.15 Gy at 1.25 MBq/mL concentration). No statistically significant biological effects were detected with the clonogenic survival assay or cell viability assay, as compared to the [135La]La-DTPA control. Qualitative SPECT imaging appeared feasible based on preliminary phantom imaging.

43045948.label: Conclusions
43045948.text: We conclude that 135La did not show therapeutic potential in combination with the respective internalizing and membrane-bound SSTR2-targeting peptides DOTA-TATE and DOTA-LM3 in vitro. The absorbed dose to the nucleus remained below levels expected to generate biological effects. Moreover, the biological response of [135La]La-DOTA-LM3 did not provide evidence for AE-induced cytotoxicity through cell membrane targeting. In addition, the high yield of low-energy X-rays complicates accurate activity quantification and nuclear imaging, which might also complicate the clinical translation. Future studies may explore 135La-labeling of DNA-binding vectors to fully take advantage of the close-range therapeutic effects of the AE-emitter 135La.

43066798.label: Purpose
43066798.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT is increasingly used after radiotherapy, even before the Phoenix threshold. We assessed the positive predictive value (PPV) of PET-positive findings in this setting.

43066798.label: Methods
43066798.text: Patients restaged with PSMA PET/CT after primary radiotherapy were classified as Phoenix-negative (PSA rise < 2.0 ng/mL above nadir) or Phoenix-positive. Local findings were verified by histopathology or MRI, metastases by histopathology or follow-up imaging. A sensitivity analysis was restricted to histopathology only. PPV was compared between Phoenix groups.

43066798.label: Results
43066798.text: Of 833 patients, 724 were PET-positive; 263 local recurrences and 219 metastatic findings had a reference standard. PPV was 83.7% for local recurrence and 95.0% for metastases. Local PPV was lower in Phoenix-negative than Phoenix-positive patients (77.7% vs. 88.1%, p = 0.029), but not with histopathological verification (84.1% vs. 86.9%); metastatic PPV did not differ between groups (96.3% vs. 94.2%).

43066798.label: Conclusion
43066798.text: Restaging PSMA PET/CT reliably identifies recurrence after radiotherapy, even before the Phoenix threshold is met.
